assumed: CPU numbering: cpu0-15 the P-cores' threads (siblings 2k, 2k+1), cpu16-31 the E-cores
core id 4k for P-core k and 32-47 for the E-cores (APIC ids 8k, and 64 + 2j for E-core j)
cluster_id 8k for P-core k and 64 + 8m for E-core module m (2 threads or 4 E-cores per L2)
cpuinfo_max_freq 5800000 on the two favoured P-cores (cpu4-7), 5500000 on the other P-cores, 4300000 on the E-cores, and the scaling_cur_freq values
No NVIDIA driver: no /proc/driver/nvidia, and nvidia-ml-py's nvmlInit fails as it does without libnvidia-ml.so.1 (NVML_ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND)
Everything outside the CPU and its sensor is a placeholder: memory, disk, NIC, addresses, /proc/stat counters, load, pressure, hostname and boot time
built: Synthesized by server/tests/synthesized_platforms.py from documented sysfs layouts and kernel source; no real device was read
device: 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900K desktop (Raptor Lake, family 6 model 183), no NVIDIA driver

sources.https://docs.kernel.org/hwmon/coretemp.h: coretemp: per-core and package sensors, crit = TjMax
sources.https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v: cpu_capacity, from drivers/base/arch_topology.c, which x86 does not build
intel_hybrid_pmu_type_map: the cpu_core, cpu_atom and cpu_lowpower PMUs
cluster_id (l2c_id): the APIC id with the L2-sharing bits cleared
temp1 "Package id N"; "Core N" of the core id at temp(core id + 2), so sparse core ids leave gaps; the docs' "Physical id" label is older text
